title: Laser Shield: a Physical Defense with Polarizer against Laser Attacks on Autonomous Driving Systems
problem: Autonomous driving systems rely on DNNs for perception but are vulnerable to physical laser attacks that can fool object detection with minimal equipment and high success rates. Existing defenses achieve low defense rates or incur prohibitive computational costs.
motivation: Laser attacks represent a critical physical-world threat to autonomous vehicle safety that current mitigation methods cannot adequately address.
method: Laser Shield uses an optical polarizer filter (a filter that only lets light vibrating in certain directions pass through) in front of the camera. The key insight is that laser-attack light and natural daylight have different polarization properties—different directions of light vibration—so the polarizer can block the attacks while preserving daylight. A mechanism automatically rotates the filter to find the angle that blocks the most attack signals while keeping images of normal scenes clear.
key_novelty: The first physical defense using a rotating optical polarizer filter to block laser attacks on autonomous driving perception.
contributions: Polarizer-based physical defense mechanism against laser attacks with low computational overhead
LAPA dataset containing physical-world laser attack scenarios for autonomous driving
Comprehensive evaluation on three baselines across four metrics demonstrating state-of-the-art defense success rate
primary_theme: optical defense against laser-based adversarial attacks
